title: Bike Demand Forecast
tagline: Predict next-hour bike rentals and beat a historical baseline without leaking the answer.
question: How accurately can we estimate next-hour rental demand?
audience: Students who know basic pandas and want their first honest forecasting project.

source.name: Bike Sharing Dataset
source.citation: Fanaee-T, H. (2013). Bike Sharing [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5W894

lesson.title: casual + registered = cnt
lesson.summary: The two user-type counts add up to the target. Feeding them to a model leaks the answer and produces a near-perfect, useless score. Weather is also an observation, not a forecast, so it is lagged by one hour.

outputs: MAE by hour: baseline vs. model

parameters.name: holdout_fraction
parameters.label: Holdout fraction
parameters.help: Share of the timeline (the most recent part) held out for evaluation.

challenges.title: Add a second model
challenges.description: Try RandomForestRegressor or a Poisson GLM on the same features.
challenges.outcome: Report holdout MAE next to the existing two.

challenges.title: Forecast 24 hours ahead
challenges.description: Drop the 1- and 2-hour lags so the model only uses information from a day earlier.
challenges.outcome: Plot how MAE grows as the horizon grows.

challenges.title: Prediction intervals
challenges.description: Fit quantile models (loss='quantile') for the 10th and 90th percentiles.
challenges.outcome: Report the share of holdout hours inside the interval.
